title: 46 Thoughts I Had About Episode 3 of 'The Shards'
text:
Lord, take me back to 1981 so I can unironically participate in roller disco.
In Episode 2, another one of Bret and his pals’ classmates—a girl named Julie Selwyn—went missing, Debbie’s dad Terry outed his own Hollywood-lothario creepiness, and a torture tape recorded by the mysterious killer stalking LA turned up at Bret’s house with Bret’s name on it.
Playing Rhonda, a…girl with Tourette’s? I mean, if anybody can pull off this role , it’s Wolk. Oh no, Wolk’s fate on this show is making me nervous, but I love this extended roller-disco solo dance sequence set to The Police’s “Don’t Stand So Close to Me” for her. Ah, jeez, I could have lived a long and happy life without seeing Ivy Wolk in a cage being fed bugs.
I love the TV logic of “a bunch of our classmates are missing, let’s have a televised dance-off! ”Okay, I do love this luxury-water-is-the-new-milk-carton gag.
“Bret, stop going to crime scenes” challenge! …that segues right into “Edge of Seventeen” by Stevie Nicks, as it should. Nope, that’s Rhonda’s captor opening her cage, and it…seems like he’s going to kill her. What’s in Jung Kook’s Bag?
